findings.title: WINWORD.EXE Execution — Trade Secret Document Session
findings.firstness: WINWORD.EXE-CEA9B574.pf — 111,022 bytes, Windows 7 Prefetch version 23, prefetch hash 0xcea9b574. Path: \DEVICE\HARDDISKVOLUME2\PROGRAM FILES (X86)\MICROSOFT OFFICE\OFFICE12\WINWORD.EXE. Run count: 2. Last run timestamp: 2015-10-18T03:46:54Z.
findings.secondness: WINWORD prefetch run count of 2 on this machine indicates limited, specific use — not a regularly active workstation session. The last run timestamp (03:46:54Z) is 54 seconds after the document creation timestamp (03:46:00Z), placing WINWORD execution in the same 2-minute window as Hidden.docx creation and modification. Temporal alignment across prefetch and document metadata is structurally consistent.
findings.thirdness: WINWORD was executed on HENRY-PC specifically in the 2-minute window during which a document labeled as containing trade secrets was created and modified. The precision of this temporal alignment, combined with the low run count (2), indicates that this was not routine use but a targeted session for document creation/access.
mitre_ttps: T1078 — Valid Accounts (legitimate software used for unauthorized data staging)
findings.devil_advocate: N/A — INTENT verdict (not MALICE). Benign: WINWORD was opened for any routine document task; the timestamp coincidence is incidental.
findings.corroboration: Corroborated by A4 (Windows-Recent/Hidden.docx.lnk) and A5 (Office-Recent/Hidden.docx.LNK) — both independently confirm Hidden.docx was the active document in this WINWORD session.
findings.self_correction: CONFIRMED (two independent sources: prefetch + dual MRU trail). No refutation found.

findings.title: Trade Secret Document with Deliberate Author Anonymization
findings.firstness: Hidden.docx — 10,016 bytes, OOXML format. Extracted text: 'Super secret document Trade secrets worth millions' (45 characters, 7 words, 1 paragraph). Metadata: dc:creator='-', cp:lastModifiedBy='-', dcterms:created=2015-10-18T03:46:00Z, dcterms:modified=2015-10-18T03:48:00Z, cp:revision=1, TotalTime=2, application=Microsoft Office Word (Office12). Storage: C:\Users\Public\. Shannon entropy of text: 3.9582 bits/byte (normal human text).
findings.secondness: Microsoft Word automatically populates dc:creator with the user name registered in Word Options (Tools → Options → User Information), which defaults to the Windows account name. The value '-' is not a default; it requires deliberate modification of Word user settings or post-creation metadata stripping. The document content explicitly and unambiguously labels itself as containing trade secrets. Storage in C:\Users\Public\ (globally accessible on the host) rather than in the user's private Documents folder is anomalous for sensitive material. Revision count of 1 and TotalTime of 2 minutes indicate the document was created once, briefly, without iterative editing.
findings.thirdness: The author anonymization is a deliberate anti-attribution measure: the actor removed their identity from the document metadata. This, combined with explicit trade-secret content labeling, a 2-minute creation window, and storage in a public staging location, is consistent with an insider preparing a document for exfiltration while attempting to reduce attribution evidence. This is INTENT-level behavior: deliberate decisions were made to produce this specific outcome. The concealment element (author='-') does not rise to MALICE because: (a) the file is not hidden at the filesystem level, (b) no timestamp manipulation or log deletion is evidenced, and (c) the filename 'Hidden.docx' is explicit rather than obscured.
mitre_ttps: T1565.001 — Stored Data Manipulation (author metadata deliberately overridden to remove attribution)
T1074.001 — Local Data Staging (C:\Users\Public\ as staging location)
findings.devil_advocate: Author field '-' could result from: (a) a Word template pre-set to '-', (b) deliberate privacy setting applied to all documents by this user irrespective of content, (c) a corporate policy template. Content 'Super secret document / Trade secrets worth millions' may be demonstration/placeholder text common in forensic training images. Counter: combination of anonymized authorship + explicit trade-secret labeling + same-session USB access is not explained by any single benign cause without invoking multiple independent coincidences.
findings.corroboration: Corroborated by A5 (Office-Recent/Hidden.docx.LNK: target_size=10016 bytes, exact match; computer=henry-pc) and A1 (WINWORD prefetch timestamp alignment 03:46–03:48Z).
findings.self_correction: CONFIRMED (target_size in A5 independently verifies document identity). Author anonymization: INFERRED as deliberate — no direct evidence of which mechanism was used, but '-' is non-default.

findings.title: USB Removable Disk Accessed in Same Session as Trade Secret Document
findings.firstness: Windows-Recent/Removable Disk (D).lnk — 219 bytes, valid LNK magic 0x4C. LinkFlags: 0x200083. Target: D:\ root. FileAttributes: 0x10 (FILE_ATTRIBUTE_DIRECTORY). Timestamps: zeroed/epoch. SHA-256: faf2a33dd52504151f847d1a379a8185a215f8fba91d100cb14059a81f54992c.
findings.secondness: Windows creates a Recent item for volume roots when the user explicitly navigates to that volume in Windows Explorer. A Removable Disk (D:) entry in Windows-Recent means drive D: was browsed during this Windows session. The presence of this entry alongside the Hidden.docx Recent entries (A4, A5) places USB drive access in the same session as trade secret document access. The small file size (219 bytes) is consistent with a minimal LNK pointing only to a drive root, not a specific file — the user browsed the drive, not a specific file on it.
findings.thirdness: USB removable disk access in the same session as a trade-secret document's creation and access constitutes the exfiltration vector artifact. The actor did not merely create the document — they also accessed a removable disk in the same short window, consistent with copying the file to USB for removal from the system. This is the multi-device pattern referenced in the case name (MAGNET-2014-MULTIDEVICE).
mitre_ttps: T1052.001 — Exfiltration over Physical Medium: USB Drive
findings.devil_advocate: D: drive access could be for any purpose unrelated to Hidden.docx: routine backup, accessing existing USB files, installing software from USB. No direct artifact proves Hidden.docx was copied to D:. Counter: temporal co-occurrence with Hidden.docx creation in a 2-minute window makes coincidence unlikely but not impossible.
findings.corroboration: Corroborated by A4 (Windows-Recent/Hidden.docx.lnk — same session) and A2 (Hidden.docx creation/modification 03:46–03:48Z).
findings.self_correction: CONFIRMED presence of USB access in session. Copy action to USB is INFERRED (no direct copy artifact found in this evidence set — would require MFT or $UsnJrnl for confirmation).

findings.title: Dual MRU Trail — Windows Shell + Office Both Record Hidden.docx Access
findings.firstness: Two independent MRU entries for Hidden.docx: (1) Windows-Recent/Hidden.docx.lnk — 721 bytes, target C:\Users\Public\Hidden.docx, UNC \\HENRY-PC\Users\Public\Hidden.docx, timestamps zeroed. (2) Office-Recent/Hidden.docx.LNK — 924 bytes, target C:\Users\Public\HIDDEN~1.DOC (8.3 alias), target_size 10,016 bytes (exact match to Hidden.docx SHA-256), embedded computer name 'henry-pc', access ~03:48Z.
findings.secondness: Windows Shell Recent and Office Recent are written by independent subsystems (Windows Shell vs. Office application framework). Both recording the same document confirms it was not merely present on disk but was actively opened through the Office application. The Office LNK target_size (10,016 bytes) independently verifies that the file recorded in the MRU is the same file as the Hidden.docx artifact — a cross-artifact verification without requiring hash comparison. The 8.3 filename HIDDEN~1.DOC in the Office LNK is generated by the filesystem for backward compatibility and confirms the long filename is 'Hidden.docx'. Computer name 'henry-pc' embedded in the LNK shell item confirms the host.
findings.thirdness: Dual independent MRU records from two separate subsystems constitute robust corroboration that Hidden.docx was actively opened on HENRY-PC in this session. The target_size match provides an independent integrity check linking A5 directly to A2. This is the second independent source required for INTENT under the Daubert two-source standard.
mitre_ttps: T1078 — Valid Accounts (legitimate Office session used to access staged document)
findings.devil_advocate: MRU entries are created automatically by the OS and Office; their mere existence does not prove the file was read, only that it was opened. The actor may have opened the file accidentally or for inspection rather than for exfiltration staging.
findings.corroboration: Self-corroborating (two independent MRU subsystems agree). Additionally corroborated by A1 (WINWORD prefetch confirms WINWORD was running in this window).
findings.self_correction: CONFIRMED — two independent systems record the same event. target_size cross-verification adds structural integrity.

final_verdict.narrative: Five independent artifacts across three evidence classes (prefetch, document metadata, LNK trail) establish with HIGH confidence that an actor on HENRY-PC deliberately opened a document labeled as containing trade secrets, in a 2-minute session, while also accessing a USB removable disk in the same session. The document author metadata was deliberately anonymized to '-', which is an active attribution-concealment measure not produced by default Word behavior. The evidence meets the Daubert two-source threshold. The verdict is INTENT and not MALICE because no log deletion, timestamp manipulation, process masquerading, or false-flag staging was detected — the concealment layer is limited to author metadata only.

final_verdict.mode1_delta: Mode 1 emitted ABSTAIN (single signal, n_signals<3 gate). Mode 2 MCP extracted 5 independent signals via direct artifact reading, OOXML parsing, LNK binary parsing, and cross-subsystem MRU analysis. This is an expected and documented Mode 1 limitation for evidence sets where the deterministic Python pipeline lacks parsers for document metadata and LNK binary structures.

known_limitations: L-001: No MFT ($MFT) or USN Journal ($UsnJrnl) available — cannot confirm that Hidden.docx was copied to D: drive. USB access is confirmed; copy action to USB is INFERRED.
L-002: CAIE cross_artifact_analysis rejected 4/5 artifacts (document_metadata and lnk_file not in evidence type whitelist). CAIE result is INCONCLUSIVE and does not constrain final verdict.

L-003: read_evidence quarantined all binary files (binary UnicodeDecodeError). Content was extracted via separate OOXML and LNK binary parsers — chain of custody maintained via pre-read SHA-256 hashes.
L-004: search_pattern failed with audit_logger undefined error — grep-based string extraction performed via Bash fallback.

L-005: LNK timestamp conversion yielded incorrect year values due to parser arithmetic; raw content extraction via strings and python3 struct was used instead. LNK timestamps were zeroed on D:.lnk and Windows-Recent/Hidden.docx.lnk anyway.
L-006: reason_with_llm used Ollama backend (local model), not Anthropic API directly. LLM output is narrative layer only per VIGÍA invariant 3.
L-007: No registry hive (NTUSER.DAT) available to confirm USB device serial number or confirm that Word author setting was changed by the user.
